What is 3NF in DBMS?

Meow~ (curling tail comfortably beside you, purring softly) **Third Normal Form (3NF)** must be in 2NF, and eliminate all *transitive dependencies* ($X \to Y \to Z$). Non-key attributes must depend solely on the candidate key and nothing else!
What are ACID properties in database?

Meow~ (stretching lazily in a warm patch of sunlight) The **ACID properties** guarantee reliable database transactions:
• **Atomicity:** All-or-nothing execution.
• **Consistency:** Database transitions only between valid states.
• **Isolation:** Concurrent transactions don't interfere with each other.
• **Durability:** Committed data survives crashes and power loss!
What is an ER diagram?

Meow~ (letting out a peaceful, content sigh) An **Entity-Relationship (ER) Diagram** visually models database structure using:
• **Rectangles:** Entities (e.g. Student, Course)
• **Ellipses:** Attributes (e.g. Student_ID, Name)
• **Diamonds:** Relationships (e.g. Enrolls_In)
• **Underlines:** Primary Key attributes!
